title: The Need for Salvation
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The need for salvation means that humanity’s deepest problem is sin before the holy God. People need rescue, forgiveness, righteousness, reconciliation, and new life, not merely improvement, advice, or relief from hardship.
summary: The need for salvation means that humanity’s deepest problem is sin before the holy God. People need rescue, forgiveness, righteousness, reconciliation, and new life, not merely improvement, advice, or relief from hardship.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Savior sinners need because He alone deals with guilt, judgment, bondage, death, and separation from God. He came to seek and save the lost, not to polish the self-sufficient.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture does not describe the human problem as merely a lack of education, opportunity, encouragement, or discipline. Those things may matter, but the root problem is sin. All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.

Sin brings guilt before God, corruption within the heart, bondage in desire, separation from God, and death. People may be wounded, weak, confused, or oppressed, but they are also morally accountable before the Lord.

Because the problem is this deep, salvation must come from God. No person can erase guilt, conquer death, make himself righteous, or create spiritual life by his own strength.

The need for salvation prepares the heart to see the greatness of Christ. Jesus did not come merely to inspire sinners, but to save them from sin and bring them back to God.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often try to define their deepest need by what hurts most in the moment. Pain, addiction, shame, loneliness, disability, poverty, and rejection are real burdens, but the Bible shows an even deeper need: sinners must be reconciled to God.

This doctrine keeps ministry from offering shallow answers. The broken need compassion, but they also need Christ. The guilty need forgiveness. The enslaved need deliverance. The dead need life.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not minimize your need before God. Confess sin honestly, refuse self-rescue, and come to Christ as the only Savior able to forgive, cleanse, restore, and give life. When helping others, offer real compassion without hiding the truth that every person’s greatest need is salvation in Jesus.
